problem_type: media delivery shape hardcoded per media kind instead of declared per provider contract
symptom: A user's relay image model (gpt-image-2.5-flare) failed integration with the raw English string 'Provider returned a pending task but the adapter has no query operation'. The failing attempt had already paid for a real image generation, the accepted upstream task was dropped without polling or cancellation, and the failure stamped meta.adapter.state=failed which removed the model from the canvas model picker entirely.
direct_cause: newapiTransportFor(kind) returned the transport recipe keyed on the media kind, and the image branch has never carried a query operation, so any relay that implements images as submit-then-poll could not be polled; the verifier then threw a non-VendorRequestError whose message reached the user verbatim.
class_root: Nomi treated 'is this media endpoint synchronous or asynchronous' as a constant of the media kind, when it is a fact each upstream declares for itself. When the real response contradicted the hardcoded assumption, the conflict was reported as an unknown upstream error rather than handled as a missing declaration on our side.
affected_population: Users connecting a self-hosted or third-party OpenAI-compatible relay whose image endpoint returns a task id instead of image data
Users connecting any future media kind through the built-in OpenAI-compatible draft
Maintainers adding a new media kind or a new relay transport recipe
entry_points: newapiTransportFor relay transport recipe used by catalog commit
buildOpenAiCompatibleDraft built-in contract for undocumented endpoints
validateProviderAdapterDraft execution boundary for AI-compiled and externally supplied contracts

external_sources.purpose: Confirm that new-api publishes create plus query for video and a synchronous images endpoint, and publishes no task cancellation endpoint.
Confirm the OpenAI-compatible images contract returns image data on the create call.
Reference asynchronous media API shape: a prediction is created, then polled, and can be cancelled.
Reference queue-based media API shape where submit and status are separate endpoints.

invariants: A transport mode declares its delivery shape explicitly; delivery is never inferred from the media kind.
A mode that declares asynchronous delivery carries both a query operation and a status mapping, or it fails the free self-check before any money is spent.

A transport recipe that declares asynchronous delivery also declares how an accepted task is abandoned: a cancel operation or poll-to-completion. Dropping an accepted task is not a permitted disposition.
A mode that declares synchronous delivery does not also carry a query operation, so there is exactly one truth about how results arrive.

The delivery declaration reaches every contract producer and reader: the AI compiler prompt, the zod contract schema handed to external agents, the catalog package format, and the published desktop-local-v1 JSON Schema.
generality_proof: Delivery is declared once in electron/catalog/transportDelivery.ts and consumed by every producer and checker: the relay recipe table asserts it at module load, the free self-check rejects an inconsistent mode, the adapter validator rejects an inconsistent AI-compiled or externally supplied contract, and the catalog package reader rejects an inconsistent imported mapping. Image, image_edit, video, image_to_video and audio each carry their own declaration rather than sharing one keyed on kind, so adding a new media kind forces a new declaration instead of silently inheriting a wrong one.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Decide, as a pure function with no network, whether one mode's delivery declaration is self-consistent.
Fail the process at module load when a transport recipe declares asynchronous delivery without a query operation, status mapping, or abandon disposition.
Hold the per-task-kind delivery declarations for the OpenAI-compatible relay family as the single source of truth.
Turn a delivery defect into a structured self-check reason before any request is sent.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Both now declare synchronous delivery explicitly, and image_edit carries its own declaration instead of relying on a shared async object that never reached it.
Both declare asynchronous delivery with the documented query endpoint, the status mapping, and a poll-to-completion abandon disposition; new-api publishes no cancel endpoint, so none is invented.
The 2026-08-30 audio fix drew this boundary at 'audio bytes'; the same declaration now covers it, so the class no longer has an audio-shaped hole and an image-shaped hole.

AI-compiled and externally supplied contracts are rejected at the execution boundary when they declare asynchronous delivery without query or statusMapping; the same requirement is emitted into the JSON Schema handed to external agents.
An imported mapping carrying an inconsistent delivery declaration is refused by the same pure function.
ComfyUI candidates execute against a local workflow runner with its own polling contract and never go through the relay transport recipes.

recurrence.reason: The identical symptom string reached users through audio on 2026-08-30 and through images on 2026-09-11. The 2026-08-30 contract drew the class boundary at 'synchronous audio bytes', which left every other media kind free to hardcode delivery by kind, so the next kind would have returned it again.
same_class_scan: Read every branch of newapiTransportFor and confirmed delivery was decided by the kind argument for image, video and audio.
Read builtinOpenAiCompatibleDraft and found image_edit never received the shared async spread that text_to_image and image_to_video received.
Read catalogCommit's relay commit path and confirmed it consumed the same recipe and propagated query only for video.

Read validateProviderAdapterDraft and the supplied-contract zod schema and confirmed neither required a delivery declaration, so an AI-compiled contract could declare a pending-task endpoint with no query.
Read catalogPackageFormat and confirmed an imported mapping had no delivery consistency check.
Read comfyuiCandidateLifecycle and confirmed it does not use the relay recipes.
Read the 2026-08-30 audio contract and confirmed its class boundary stopped at audio response bytes.

prevention.invariant: Delivery shape is declared per upstream contract, and an asynchronous declaration must carry a query operation, a status mapping, and an abandon disposition.
prevention.failure_mode: A transport recipe that violates the invariant throws at module load, so the process cannot start; a mode-level violation fails the free self-check, the adapter validator, and the catalog package reader before any request is sent.
prevention.strategy: Move delivery from an argument-keyed branch into an explicit per-task-kind declaration table, assert the invariant where the table is defined, and have every producer and reader of a mode contract consult the same pure checker.

invariant_owner_layer.rationale: The invariant belongs to the transport-recipe derivation layer, not to the verifier. The verifier only discovered the conflict; it never owned the declaration, which is exactly why the 2026-08-30 fix at the verifier boundary did not stop the image recurrence.

legacy_paths.rationale: The kind-keyed delivery branch, the hand-sprinkled shared async object in the built-in draft, and the paid create-poll-download verification path are deleted in the same commit. No callable fallback retains the old interpretation.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The invariant is owned by Nomi's own transport declarations and does not depend on a third-party package version.

migration: No catalog migration is required. Mappings persisted before this change carry no delivery field and are interpreted by the documented backward-compatible inference: a mapping with a query operation is asynchronous, one without is synchronous. That is exactly the behaviour those rows already had.
residual_risks: A relay whose image endpoint is asynchronous still cannot be polled until someone supplies its query endpoint, because new-api publishes none for images and inventing one would violate R5. The difference is that the user now learns this for free, in plain language, with a working next step, instead of after paying for a dropped generation.
new-api publishes no task cancellation endpoint, so the video abandon disposition is poll-to-completion rather than an explicit cancel.
